proof:
# Full active rank is impossible with a full row at an unpaid stochastic maximum

This is an all-dimensional structural theorem for simplex capacities. It does not prove stochastic containment or OC; maxima with fewer active rows remain possible obligations.

Let d>=2 and m=d+1. For the uniform barycentric probability U on the d-simplex define

    phi_d(x)=inf_{t>0,Pr(x dot U<=t)>0} t/Pr(x dot U<=t)^(1/d), x>=0.

Fix strictly positive weights c_i and maximize H(X)=sum_i c_i phi_d(X_i) over nonnegative m-square matrices whose columns each sum to one. Choose a maximizer with the least number k of nonzero rows. Its nonzero rows are linearly independent, by the scaling argument in `candidate f62fe2e83b180bf3`.

**Theorem.** If k=m and at least one row is strictly positive in every coordinate, the capacity vector is an already-paid unit vector or the matrix cannot be a maximizer. Equivalently every unpaid minimal-active maximum with a full row has k<=d.

## 1. Regularity and the common multiplier vector

The full-cut exclusion in `candidate 78b95c208ba2d374` shows that every full row of an unpaid maximum has a unique proper threshold. The all-dimensional theorem in `candidate a5d3d44181ebed82` proves that its capacity is C2, and that the threshold minimum is nondegenerate. Its gradient is F_i^(-1/d)b^(i), where b^(i) is the actual section centroid in barycentric coordinates and has all entries positive.

A nonzero row with two or more zero entries cannot coexist with such a full row: decrease one of its positive entries by epsilon and give it to the full row. Its capacity stays zero, while the full row increases to first order by a strictly positive gradient coordinate. Therefore every nonzero nonfull row has exactly one zero.

Column transfers between full rows give a common strictly positive weighted gradient lambda. Transfers at the positive entries of one-zero rows identify their derivatives with the same lambda. Put S=sum_j lambda_j and b=lambda/S. All full-row section centroids equal b. Their thresholds are t_i=X_i dot b. Define this t_i for every active row; it is positive for every such row and sums to one over all rows.

For clarity, the restriction imposed by a one-zero row is included explicitly. If its missing column is h, its capacity is the geometric mean g of its d positive entries. Writing mu=c_i g/d, equality of positive-coordinate derivatives gives X_ij=mu/lambda_j for j!=h. The exact inward derivative at its zero is

    c_i partial_(0+) phi_d
       =d max_(j!=h)lambda_j-sum_(j!=h)lambda_j.

This follows from the elementary first-threshold expansion proved in `candidate 6a014eb26413a72b`: for entries (epsilon,a_1,...,a_d), the derivative is GM(a)[1/min(a)-(sum 1/a_j)/d]. Funding that entry from a full row forces it to be at most lambda_h. Consequently

    b_j<=1/d for all j!=h.                          (1)

## 2. Noncentral coordinates and a paying full-row direction

Let I={j:b_j>1/d}. For every proper full-row section all indices in I lie on the same strict side. This follows from the actual log-concave exponential density: if ell=f_V'(0)/f_V(0), a positive margin at an index in I forces ell<0 by the density's tangent bound, while a negative margin at such an index forces ell>0. A zero margin has b_j=1/d. Thus opposite strict signs within I are impossible. This proof, including zero margins, is in Section 6 of the Schur source.

If I is empty, any full row captures at least two central vertices. If |I|>=2, (1) excludes all one-zero rows, so all active rows are full. Choose h in I. The full-row margins t_i-X_ih sum to zero. None is zero, since b_h>1/d. Therefore some full row has a negative margin at h; the same-side property makes all its margins at I negative. Its at least two strictly captured vertices are consequently central.

If I={h}, every one-zero row must miss h. Its margin at h equals t_i>0. The sum of all row margins at h is zero. If any one-zero row exists, the full-row margins have strictly negative sum. If none exists, all full-row margins are nonzero and sum to zero. In both cases some full row strictly excludes h and hence captures at least two central vertices.

We have obtained in every case a full row whose minimizing cap strictly captures two coordinates at most 1/d. The audited reciprocal-transform cap lemma supplies a negative tangent cap-curvature direction. The explicit common-shift correction in the Schur source turns this into strictly positive optimized-capacity curvature. The correction includes the full threshold Schur term and is valid in every d>=2.

## 3. Rank contradiction and residual scope

At k=m the independent active rows span R^m. The direction just constructed can therefore be funded by proportional scalings of the active rows while preserving every column sum. The exact projective-variation identity cancels the linear objective term and leaves a strictly positive quadratic term. This contradicts maximality and proves the theorem.

The only exception used above is the full-cut row saturating d columns, whose capacity vector is a unit vector explicitly realized by a zero-diagonal stochastic matrix. The d=1 problem is handled separately and is not inferred from threshold nondegeneracy.

More generally, at any minimal-active maximum with common b_j<=1/d for all j, let f be the number of full rows. Each has at least one positive Hessian direction. The joint funding lemma in `candidate 58f8bbb67f63ee23` then gives k+f<=d+1. This is a necessary index bound, not a proof of the remaining lower-rank cases. In particular the two-full-row/one-zero-row tetrahedral configuration with one noncentral hole is not eliminated here.
